question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Mad as a hatter
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Mad as a hatter"** means to be **completely crazy** or insane. (पूरी तरह से पागल)

 
 
• **Example: **After spending hours in the sun without a hat, he started acting as mad as a hatter.
 
 
 
• **"Completely Crazy"** refers to someone who is out of their mind or not thinking rationally. (पूरी तरह से पागल)
 
 
• **Example: **She must be** completely crazy** to think she can finish the project in one day.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom **'Mad as a hatter'** is equivalent to **'Completely Crazy'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be alert** (चौकस होना): Being watchful and attentive to potential dangers or problems.

 
 
• **Example:** You need to be alert while crossing the busy street.
 
 
 
• **To cause trouble** (मुसीबत खड़ी करना): Creating problems or disturbances.
 
 
• **Example:** He loves to cause trouble wherever he goes.
 
 
 
• **Fast asleep** (गहरी नींद में): Sleeping very deeply.
 
 
• **Example:** The baby was fast asleep in her crib.
 
 

37:Tc40,

The correct answer is: **Option 1.**
